title: How to change a system without regressing related in-scope features

authority.reference: Owner direction, 2026-10-23: agents must check related in-scope features before and after a system change; a new feature or local repair must not silently regress them.

applies_to: source, data, configuration, invariant, interface, interaction, simulation, lifecycle, build, test, and runtime-behavior changes
repairs and feature introductions as well as deliberate refactors
CodeExp2 and every target repository established or resumed through CodeExp2
does_not_apply_to: ordinary prose-only edits with no operational, instruction, acceptance, interface, or runtime effect
scope.not_a_loophole: Renaming a system change as a refactor, tuning, cleanup, data change, test-only change, local fix, or documentation does not remove this rule when it can alter an in-scope behavior or its verification.

invariant.rule: Before editing an in-scope system, identify the existing related features that can be affected. Before claiming success, committing, or advancing dependent work, verify the changed behavior and every identified related feature against the exact candidate. A new behavior passing by itself is never evidence that related behavior was preserved.
invariant.fail_closed: Unknown related behavior, an untested related behavior, absent evidence, an empty inventory without discovery evidence, or a suspected regression is a preservation failure. Do not call the change PASS, do not commit it through a preservation-required gate, and do not advance dependent work.
invariant.owner_change_boundary: A related feature may change only with an explicit owner decision that names the changed behavior and acceptance replacement. An agent may not call a regression intentional merely because it simplifies an implementation.

required_workflow.name: Map the change surface before editing
required: State the requested behavior and exact system boundary.
Inspect the plan, acceptance criteria, current behavior, source dependencies, tests, runtime paths, and relevant prior failures.
List direct counterparts, adjacent modes, opposite-direction cases, shared state, fallback/recovery paths, and user-visible flows that the change can affect.
Use repository evidence; author memory, a ticket title, or a new-feature description is not a complete inventory.
prohibited: Assuming a nearby feature is irrelevant because the edited branch is different.
Treating absence of a named test as proof that no related behavior exists.

required_workflow.name: Define preservation checks before implementation
required: For each inventory item, define a candidate-source check that distinguishes preserved behavior from regression.
Use the real interaction when the behavior is user-visible; focused deterministic tests complement but do not replace a required runtime check.
Include at least one counterpart case whenever a classifier, threshold, shared handler, collision/contact rule, state transition, or common fallback is changed.
Bind every check to the exact candidate source, not unstaged repairs or historical green results.
prohibited: One happy-path assertion presented as system coverage.
Rebaselining an old expected result to hide a regression.

required_workflow.name: Verify both the requested change and preserved behavior
required: Run the requested-change check and all preservation checks after the edit.
Inspect failures as evidence of a changed behavior, not as noise from a nearby feature.
If a related feature regresses, stop the claim, preserve the failure, update the inventory, and repair the common owner or explicitly obtain an owner decision for an intentional product change.
prohibited: Closing a repair because the original bug is fixed while a related behavior now fails.
Moving on to a next step, commit, or runtime qualification while a known related regression remains.

required_workflow.name: Produce a truthful preservation receipt
required: Name the changed system boundary and exact candidate source identity.
Name each related feature, why it is related, its preservation status, and the exact evidence/check that was run.
State every limitation and unknown explicitly; UNKNOWN is not PASS.
For an intentional owner-authorized change, include the owner decision reference and replacement acceptance check.
Make the receipt available to the existing plan, handover, review, or commit gate that owns the change; do not create a parallel tracking system.
required_workflow.required_attestation: I inspected the related in-scope features and their candidate-source checks. I am not claiming preservation for any unknown, untested, failed, or owner-unapproved behavior.

receipt_contract.use_existing_record: Use the repository's existing plan, change record, test manifest, review record, or gate-policy receipt field. Do not add a database, daemon, or parallel workflow only for this receipt.
minimum_fields: related_features with stable IDs, relation, status, and check/evidence
owner decision reference for every intentionally changed related feature
receipt_contract.pass: Every discovered related feature is preserved or has an explicit owner-authorized replacement. Every declared check passed against the exact candidate. At least one counterpart-preservation check is distinct from the requested-change check. No feature is failed or unknown.
receipt_contract.not_pass: An omitted counterpart, a counterpart check reused from the requested-change check, a guessed inventory, a test that exercises only new behavior, a stale receipt, a check against different bytes, or a generic assertion that no regression occurred.

commit_gate_integration.rule: Every repository that CodeExp2 establishes, resumes, or drives for a system change must have an additive pre-commit or equivalent candidate-source admission boundary. Its reviewed policy must require a feature-preservation receipt for each admitted system-change scope and require the receipt's preservation tests in the exact staged run. A target with no usable native hook is setup_required, not exempt.
commit_gate_integration.CodeExp2_consumer: The candidate scripts/check_staged.py validates feature_preservation_receipts in a preservation-enabled reviewed policy and runs the declared tests from the index snapshot. It becomes local hook enforcement only after the repository's required independent review and adoption.
commit_gate_integration.additive_boundary: Add this validation inside the existing candidate-source verifier reached by the repository's current hook. Preserve the current bootstrap, hook path, policy pins, redirected-input checks, instruction protections, reviewed-inventory checks, staged snapshot construction, mandatory regressions, and rejection behavior. Replacing the hook, bypassing it, or treating the receipt as a substitute for an existing check is forbidden.
commit_gate_integration.limit: A gate can prove the receipt is complete, mapped to the staged scope, and its declared checks passed. It cannot prove an agent discovered every real-world behavior; the mandatory pre-edit inventory and review remain the defense against omission.
commit_gate_integration.no_bypass: Do not relabel an operational change as ordinary documentation, omit a receipt, use a stale receipt, or use an unstaged test repair. These are commit-blocking failures where the gate applies.

cross_repository_adoption.required: On every mission creation, establishment, resumption, connection, attachment, or dispatch attempt, require the Feature Preservation hook activation receipt before the mission can become active. Registration may exist as inactive coordination metadata, but no builder attachment, target-agent connection, system-change work, commit, or product dispatch is eligible without the receipt.
cross_repository_adoption.target_gate_rule: Use the target's existing commit/CI/admission mechanism. Extend its smallest staged-source or equivalent candidate boundary; preserve every prior hook command and its refusal behavior. If the target has no usable boundary, create the smallest native additive pre-commit installation through its supported setup route before CodeExp2-driven system-change work or commits. Do not copy CodeExp2's local hook, replace an existing hook, or invent a generic enforcement service.
cross_repository_adoption.handoff_requirement: Assignments for system changes must name the preservation inventory, counterpart checks, receipt destination, and stop condition for a discovered regression.
cross_repository_adoption.host_adoption_receipt: Record the actual hook path, preserved prior commands, receipt validator/policy location, passing candidate-source run, failing missing-receipt run, builder ACK, and limits. A source guide link, hook-file copy, or local policy without those observed results is setup_required. This is the mission activation receipt: absent, stale, mismatched, or failed means INACTIVE and forbids attachment, connection, dispatch, system work, and commit.

consumer.discovery: CodeExp2 AGENTS.md reusable-agent-instructions table, Delivery Discipline, plan guide, and mission handoff route.
consumer.semantic_consumer: Coordinator and target builders before edits, advancement, claims, and commits.
consumer.runtime_enforcement: Agent-interpreted before-edit and review obligations. Actual commit enforcement is supplied by each repository's existing candidate-source gate; CodeExp2's candidate is scripts/check_staged.py and requires independent review/adoption before activation.

completion_checks: A system change has a non-empty evidence-based related-feature inventory before implementation.
Each inventory item has a candidate-source preservation check and outcome.
The requested behavior and meaningful counterpart behaviors have passed their checks.
Known failures and unknowns block PASS, advancement, and required commit-gate admission.
The current target's existing gate, not a new parallel system, is the effect boundary for its staged-source receipt.
